Efficacious

ef-ih-KAY-shuhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Efficacious is capable of producing the desired result -- it describes a treatment, plan, or remedy that reliably does what it was meant to do.

The charity's efficacious use of donations meant nearly every dollar reached families in need.

Worked Example

The city's efficacious new recycling program cut landfill waste by nearly forty percent in its first year.

The program didn't just exist -- it actually produced the exact result it was designed for, which is what makes something efficacious rather than merely well-intentioned.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

effective: Effective is the everyday word for anything that works -- a plan, a speech, a mousetrap -- even one that works only partly or only once. Efficacious is its formal cousin with a stricter claim: it reliably produces the exact result intended, and it is the version medical and scientific writing reaches for.

potent: Potent measures raw strength -- a potent medicine or argument hits hard. It says nothing about aim: a potent drug can overwhelm a patient without curing the illness it was given for. Efficacious is judged on outcome alone: whatever its force, it produces the exact result that was intended.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

ineffective: not producing the intended result

futile: incapable of producing any useful result

Where it sits · how reliably it gets results — adequate → efficacious → infallible

adequate vs. efficacious: Adequate is weaker than efficacious: an adequate remedy is merely satisfactory, while an efficacious one works more powerfully, reliably producing the exact result you wanted.

infallible vs. efficacious: Infallible goes further than efficacious: an efficacious treatment usually produces the desired result, but an infallible one is more absolute, since it never fails at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — efficacy

root — efficacy: the ability to produce a desired result (from Latin efficere, 'to accomplish') (Latin efficere)

suffix — -ious

suffix — -ious: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Efficacious is efficacy ('the ability to produce a desired result') plus -ious, 'full of.' Something efficacious is full of that accomplishing power -- it actually works.
